_comment: Whether a wallet-signed forum request (the sign-in, the in-app report, the activity read) may leave the device now, from the tunnel's state alone. The POST rides a protected socket that bypasses the tunnel, but the connect host name is still resolved by the system resolver, which no protector covers: while the tunnel is coming up or going down the resolver points at the tunnel DNS and the lookup times out, and while the kill switch holds a blocking interface there is no resolver at all. Those states defer, and the deferral names its class for the journal and nothing else. Written against the behaviour at HEAD; readers and skip lists in README.md.

cases.name: disconnected
cases._comment: No tunnel at all: the physical resolver answers.

cases.name: connected
cases._comment: Settled: the protected socket leaves and the resolver answers.

cases.name: disconnecting_to_reconnect
cases._comment: A disconnect that is the first half of a reconnect is named for where it is going, not for the half it is in.

cases.name: blocking
cases._comment: The kill switch holds a blocking interface: no resolver at all, so the lookup fails at once.

cases.name: failed_released
cases._comment: Terminal and released: the tunnel is closed, no reconnect is scheduled and the physical resolver answers. It is also the state a person most wants to report from, and deferring it refused the report in exactly the failure it described. iOS has no such state: its error state blocks rather than releasing, and is the `blocking` case.
